acs: AC-1: Given a repo/project with stored user_profile/agent_profile aggregates, entity relations, and a fixture set of decisions/lessons/todos, When the get_suggestions MCP tool is called scoped to that repo, Then it returns at most 5 ranked suggestions, each citing the memory id(s) it derives from, ranked by the existing fuse signals (recency/importance/usefulness) with no new ranking model introduced.

AC-2: Given the same tool call, When the top-ranked candidate's confidence score falls below a configured threshold (e.g. suggestions.minConfidence: 0.5), Then that suggestion is silently dropped (not down-ranked); Given every candidate falls below threshold, Then get_suggestions returns an empty list, and the drop event is logged as a structured entry (observability).

AC-3: Given contracts/manifests/mcp-tools.v1.json, When get_suggestions is added, Then tests/contracts/mcp-tool-manifest-parity.test.ts and tests/mcp/server.test.ts both pass against the live tools/list wire response.

AC-4: Given a config-gated session-start integration point (suggestions.sessionStart.enabled, default true, cap <=5, silent below threshold), When a new session starts with no suggestions clearing the confidence bar, Then no suggestion payload is emitted at all; Given the flag is false, Then the session-start path is byte-identical to pre-FEAT-545 behavior (reliability).

AC-5: Given a small gold fixture set under tests/, When the suggestion assembly logic runs against each fixture, Then the actual suggestion set matches the gold set for every fixture, and at least one fixture asserts the AC-2 silent-below-threshold behavior explicitly.

AC-6: Given a user acts on or dismisses a suggestion, When that action is recorded, Then the existing recall_used/correction-style usefulness signal is emitted with the cited memory id(s); Given a suggestion is dismissed 3 consecutive times for the same memory id, Then a regression test proves that memory id's suggestion-ranking score decays.

acs: AC-1: Given a seeded 28-day history of ingest sessions, When each of at least 4 detectors runs (ingest-shape collapse, contradiction/correction-rate spike, duplicate-pressure surge, provenance/capture-source-mix shift), Then each computes a rate against its own trailing-window baseline (28-day median +/- MAD) rather than a hardcoded absolute threshold.

AC-2: Given fewer than a configured minimum number of historical windows, When a detector runs, Then it reports inconclusive: true with reason ('denominator unavailable') rather than a false-negative or false-positive alarm off an unstable baseline.

AC-3: Given the anomaly detectors, When doctor runs, Then each is registered as a Check tagged tier: 'cheap' or 'full' appropriately, and When `astramem-local memory anomalies` CLI runs, Then it lists every firing anomaly with the numbers behind each plus a structured JSON output mode.

AC-4: Given a seeded history engineered to contain exactly one anomaly, When the corresponding detector runs, Then it fires; given a seeded history with normal variance within learned MAD tolerance, When the same detector runs, Then it stays silent — both asserted in the same test file.
AC-5: Given a detector fires, When it logs, Then the log entry is structured and includes detector name, measured rate, learned baseline, and deviation magnitude (in MADs).

AC-5: Given mode: 'enabled' but no rewrite variant clears a minimum relevance bar, When search() runs, Then it falls back to the original-query-only path silently (not an error).
